meta.triageRationale: One cohesive story under a single design, but it spans the config layer, provider routing, the CLI provider's argument building for two CLIs, and three settings surfaces in three codebases (TS TUI, VS Code extension, Kotlin JetBrains plugin). It carries real design choices: the effort vocabulary per CLI (codex -c model_reasoning_effort vs claude --effort, both low/medium/high/xhigh/max), how an effort the runner does not support is handled (ollama), byRepo overrides, and how the catalog/manifest declare a new optional enum per tier. More than one build task. Not an epic: no new subsystem, one story.

findings.premise: The user's decision that effort is set on the global tiers only (no per-repo effort) is designed: parseTieringOverride reads effort only on the global scope, warns and ignores it under byRepo, and the router takes effort from the global tier even when a byRepo tier supplies runner/model.
findings.evidence: parseTiering (src/config/analyze.ts:381-394) calls parseTieringOverride(models,'global') and parseTieringOverride(entry, 'byRepo[<repo>]'), so the where argument already tells the two scopes apart. The router uses configuredTier = byRepo?.tiers?.[tier] ?? cfg.tiering.tiers?.[tier] (role-router.ts:135), and cfg.tiering.tiers is always fully resolved by assembleConfig (analyze.ts:256), so the global tier's effort can be read separately. Design sections 2.3/2.4 and the edge cases cover this. The Story declares no ACs; the derived ac1-ac4 cover parsing, passing the effort to the CLI, unchanged behaviour when unset, and every settings surface. None of them builds a per-repo effort. [files: src/config/analyze.ts, src/analyze/context/role-router.ts]

DEFAULT_TIERS.core. The catalog default for core.model is '' (config-catalog.ts:114), so after reconcile the core tier is dropped. That is the case the design's efforts side-map exists for. q8faa690b.question: Resolved (user, 2026-10-23): no per-repo effort. The effort is set only on the global model tiers; per-repo config only chooses which tier a function uses.
q8faa690b.choice: Effort on global tiers only (as resolved)
q8faa690b.rationale: User 2026-10-23: no per-repo override; per-repo config only chooses which tier a function uses.

summary.prose: Each global model tier (core, mid, cheap) gains an optional reasoning effort: low, medium, high, xhigh or max. When a tier runs on the claude or codex CLI, insrc passes that effort to the CLI with its own flag; when it is unset, the call is exactly as today. The effort belongs to the global tiers only: a per-repo entry cannot set it, and every function resolved to a tier runs at that tier's global effort. The effort is declared in the config catalog, so the insrc TUI tier pane, the VS Code settings and tier picker, and the JetBrains model-tiers section can all show and set it beside the tier's runner and model.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Add a per-tier reasoning-effort setting to model tiers

api.name: TierModel
api.signature: interface TierModel { readonly runner: AnalyzeShaperProviderKind; readonly model: string; readonly effort?: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max' | undefined }

parameters.name: effort
parameters.purpose: New. The reasoning effort the tier's CLI runs at; absent means the CLI's own default

returns.meaning: Carried from config through the role router to the provider

postconditions: A tier without effort is exactly today's TierModel

api.name: parseTieringOverride
api.signature: function parseTieringOverride(src: Record<string, unknown>, where: string): TieringOverride  // unchanged signature; also reads val['effort'] on the global scope

parameters.name: src
parameters.purpose: The global models section or one byRepo entry, as today

returns.meaning: Each valid global tier now carries effort when the config sets one of the five values

errors.condition: a global tier's effort is present but not '' and not one of low|medium|high|xhigh|max: the effort alone is dropped with a warning naming the tier; the tier keeps its runner and model
a models.byRepo[repo].tiers.<tier> entry carries an effort: the effort is ignored with a warning saying effort is set on the global tiers only; the byRepo tier's runner and model apply as today

postconditions: '' or absent effort leaves the tier without effort
Only the global scope reads effort; parseTiering's byRepo entries never carry one

api.name: RoleResolution
api.signature: interface RoleResolution { readonly role: string; readonly tier: TierName; readonly runner: AnalyzeShaperProviderKind; readonly model: string; readonly effort?: TierModel['effort']; readonly clampedByFloor: boolean }

parameters.name: effort
parameters.purpose: New. The effort of the GLOBAL tier the role resolves to (models.tiers.<tier>.effort, including its DEFAULT_TIERS fallback), also when a byRepo tier supplies the runner and model; the router passes it on as roleEffort to buildShaperProvider

returns.meaning: Read by materialize (src/analyze/context/role-router.ts) and by resolveValidateProvider (src/daemon/steps/build-step/phases/validate.ts)

postconditions: The effort always comes from the global tier of the resolved tier name; a per-repo override changes which tier a role uses or that tier's runner/model, never its effort
materialize always forwards it to buildShaperProvider as roleEffort, as null when the tier has no effort, so the routed path never falls back to cfg.shaperEffort

api.name: ShaperProviderOverrides
api.signature: interface ShaperProviderOverrides { /* existing fields */ readonly roleEffort?: TierModel['effort'] | null }

parameters.name: roleEffort
parameters.purpose: New. Set by the role router's materialize on every routed call: the resolved global tier's effort, or null when that tier has none (routed, no effort flag). Absent only for the callers outside the router (code-review-rpc defaultProvider, workflow-rpc's run-wide provider, docgen's narrative-generator), which run at the global core tier's effort, cfg.shaperEffort

postconditions: buildShaperProvider's effort: roleEffort when it is a value; none when roleEffort is null; cfg.shaperEffort only when roleEffort is absent (a non-router caller)
A routed mid or cheap role never inherits the core tier's effort: with core at max and mid unset, a mid role sends no effort flag
A repo override (repoOverride) changes the runner as today but not the effort
The effort reaches CliProvider only on buildShaperProvider's CLI branch; the Ollama branch ignores it
buildSummariserProvider passes cfg.summariserEffort to its CliProvider

parameters.name: effort
parameters.purpose: New. The reasoning effort for every invocation of this provider

returns.meaning: Stored by the CliProvider constructor and read by modelArgs

returns.meaning: Today's ['--model', model] (or []) followed by the effort flag: claude ['--effort', effort]; codex ['-c', `model_reasoning_effort=${effort}`]; nothing when effort is unset

postconditions: Every invocation that uses modelArgs (complete, completeStructuredOnce, runEditSession, and both review sessions through claudeReviewSessionArgs and codexReviewSessionArgs) carries the effort
Without effort the argv is byte-identical to today's

api.signature: unchanged; builds new CliProvider({ kind, model, effort: resolution.effort })

errorCases.scenario: The config sets a tier's effort to a value that is not one of '', low, medium, high, xhigh, max (a typo such as 'hgh', a number, an object)
errorCases.detection: parseTieringOverride checks val['effort'] against the five values and ''
errorCases.response: Log a warning naming the tier and the value; drop only the effort; keep the tier's runner and model
errorCases.userImpact: That tier runs at the CLI's default effort and the warning in the daemon log says why

errorCases.scenario: A per-repo tier entry (models.byRepo[repo].tiers.<tier>) carries an effort
errorCases.detection: parseTieringOverride, parsing a byRepo entry, finds an effort key on a tier
errorCases.response: Ignore the effort and log a warning saying effort is set on the global model tiers only; the byRepo tier's runner and model apply as today
errorCases.userImpact: The functions of that repo run at the global tier's effort; the warning says why the per-repo value had no effect

errorCases.scenario: A model refuses an effort insrc passed (insrc passes only low, medium, high, xhigh or max, checked when the config is parsed)
errorCases.detection: codex rejects an unsupported value with HTTP 400 'Invalid value ... Supported values are ...' and exits 1 (probed with codex 0.164: an unknown value exits 1); CliProvider's existing failure handling reads its stderr. claude does not fail: with an unknown --effort value it warns 'Unknown --effort value ... ignoring it and using the default effort' and exits 0 (probed)
errorCases.response: codex: the call fails as any CLI failure does today, with codex's message in the error (no retry without the effort, no silent downgrade). claude: the call runs at claude's default effort and its warning is in the CLI's stderr
errorCases.userImpact: A codex run or review on that tier fails with codex's message and the user lowers or clears the effort; a claude tier runs at its default effort

errorCases.scenario: A settings surface sets an effort while the daemon is older than this change (its catalog has no effort rows)
errorCases.detection: VS Code: nothing detects it; the native setting and the tier picker come from the plugin's own manifest and bundled catalog, and the write goes through config.write, which stores any path. JetBrains: ModelTiersModel finds no models.tiers.<tier>.effort row in the catalog the daemon serves
errorCases.response: VS Code shows the effort control and the write is stored; the older daemon parses only runner and model and ignores the key. JetBrains shows no effort combo for that tier and writes nothing
errorCases.userImpact: With an older daemon a VS Code effort has no effect until the daemon is updated, after which the stored value applies without being set again; JetBrains offers the control once the daemon is updated

migration.stateBefore: A tier is { runner, model } (src/config/analyze.ts:106-109); parseTieringOverride ignores any other key (:341-375), so an effort in config has no effect. CliProvider's modelArgs adds only --model (src/agent/providers/cli-provider.ts:505-515), and the CLIs run at their own default effort (codex: ~/.codex/config.toml, global). The catalog has two rows per tier (src/config/config-catalog.ts:113-118); the TUI pane, the VS Code manifest and tier picker and the JetBrains ModelTiersSection edit runner and model only (s1: TUI, VS Code and JetBrains bundles).
migration.stateAfter: Each global tier may carry effort (low|medium|high|xhigh|max); the router and buildShaperProvider/buildSummariserProvider/resolveValidateProvider hand the global tier's effort to CliProvider, which passes --effort (claude) or -c model_reasoning_effort (codex); a per-repo entry cannot set it. Three catalog rows declare it with default '' (CLI default); the TUI, VS Code (native settings and tier picker) and JetBrains model-tiers section show and set it.

migrationSteps.action: Add the optional effort to TierModel and parse it on the global tiers (also recording it for a tier that falls back to DEFAULT_TIERS); invalid values are dropped alone with a warning, and an effort under a byRepo tier is ignored with a warning

Carry the global tier's effort through RoleResolution, ShaperProviderOverrides.roleEffort, AnalyzeConfig (shaperEffort, summariserEffort, derived in assembleConfig; resolveTiers carries a global tier's effort onto its DEFAULT_TIERS fallback), buildSummariserProvider, resolveSummariser and resolveValidateProvider into CliProviderOpts; CliProvider's modelArgs appends the CLI's effort flag when set
Declare the three catalog rows (enum with '' default) and raise the contract test's row count to 48; reconcile fills effort: '' into existing configs on the next daemon boot
TUI: add an effort row per tier to ModelTiersPane (tierFieldPath gains 'effort'; row count and indices move to three per tier)
VS Code: add the three manifest entries mirroring the catalog and an effort step to the tier picker
JetBrains: add effort to ModelTiersModel's TierState and writes, and an effort combo to ModelTiersSection
Update the installed daemon and set models.tiers.core.effort = high and models.tiers.mid.effort = medium in ~/.insrc/config.json (the motivating configuration)

migration.backwardCompat: Additive. TierModel, TieringOverride, RoleResolution, ShaperProviderOverrides, AnalyzeConfig and CliProviderOpts gain optional fields; callers that set none get today's argv byte for byte. Existing configs gain effort: '' (unset) through reconcile's fill. An older daemon ignores an effort key a newer surface wrote (it parsed only runner/model). An effort under a byRepo tier is ignored with a warning.

alternativesConsidered.name: Optional effort on TierModel, declared as catalog enum rows
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: TierModel gains an optional effort; three catalog enum rows models.tiers.<tier>.effort (values '', low, medium, high, xhigh, max; default '' = the CLI's own default) drive every settings surface; the effort travels with the runner/model to CliProvider, which adds the CLI's own flag.

alternativesConsidered.name: Undeclared optional key, read only by the daemon
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Parse models.tiers.<tier>.effort in the daemon and pass it to the CLI, without catalog rows; each settings surface special-cases the key.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Meets the CLI side but only partly the every-surface constraint.

alternativesConsidered.name: Effort encoded in the model id
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Write the effort into the model string (e.g. 'gpt-6.1-sol@high'); the CLI provider splits it.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Cheapest, but overloads the model id and still needs picker work while losing validation.

openQuestions: ts1 (partial): the Story declares no acceptanceCriteria; the test strategy maps four criteria (ac1-ac4) derived from the story text: per-tier parsing on the global tiers, passing the effort to the CLI, unchanged behaviour when unset, and every settings surface.
Resolved (user, 2026-10-23): no per-repo effort. The effort is set only on the global model tiers; per-repo config only chooses which tier a function uses.
